messages:
maya: Heads up — hitting a weird edge in the Node SDK when running in JSON mode + auth retry. Our sampleapp's function-calling path returns an object but after a retry it becomes a JSON string literal (escaped) and then the schema validator rejects it.

ryan: ugh. can you paste the failing payload + schema? does python sdk behave the same?

maya: repro below. Node SDK v0.9.3, sampleapp v0.4.5. Python (v0.9.3) returns the object like you'd expect. Node shows the body double-serialized when the auth retry fires.

maya: ```
# schema (simplified)
{"type":"object","properties":{"task":{"type":"string"},"result":{"type":"object","properties":{"score":{"type":"number"}}},"required":["task","result"]}
```

maya: failing response (what Node hands to validator):
```json
"{
  \"task\": \"summarize\",
  \"result\": \"{\\\"score\\\": 0.87}\"
}"
```

maya: note result is a string containing a JSON object, not an object. The validator then says result is not an object.

jen: that screams retry path stringification. We had a similar pattern in an older helper where we wrapped responses for logging and accidentally JSON.stringified before returning. Is the retry wrapper using JSON.stringify for safe logging?

maya: looks like it. Traced to auth/refresh retry middleware: it serializes body for the queued retry, but when we rehydrate the request we don't parse it back. Python's retry keeps the body as native object, so parity bug.

ryan: can you paste minimal log lines? especially request->retry->rehydrate bits.

maya: log snip: ```
[2024-10-03T17:22:10.123Z] INFO retry: queued request {method: POST, body: '{"task":"summarize","result":{"score":0.87}}'}
[2024-10-03T17:22:10.456Z] INFO retry: rehydrating body from queue -> body: '{"task":"summarize","result":"{\"score\":0.87}"}'
```

jen: yep. queue is storing stringified body and rehydrate is not restoring nested objects. Fix is either store parsed object or avoid stringifying nested objects. Might be okay to special-case application/json and JSON.parse on rehydrate.

ryan: quick workaround for sampleapp: add a post-validate hook that json-parses result if typeof result === 'string'. Ugly but buys time. Also add a unit test to catch this parity difference.

maya: we've got a simple workaround that does: ```js
if (typeof res.result === 'string') { try { res.result = JSON.parse(res.result) } catch (e) { /* noop */ } }
```
but want canonical SDK fix.

devex-bot: Created issue REDWOOD-ISSUE-1289: "node-sdk: auth retry path double-serializes structured outputs (JSON mode parity)" — https://redwood/issues/1289

jen: I'll open a PR to the node-sdk. Plan: detect content-type application/json and keep body as object in retry queue. Add integration test that uses functioncall schema with nested object and forces auth refresh.

ryan: ping me on the PR for test design. we should also add a smoke parity test against python so CI can catch regressions.

ci-bot: Failing job - integration/structured-output-parity (sampleapp) — see job id 4523. Marking flaky = false.

maya: created a small repro branch and added a failing test that demonstrates the double-stringify. dropping link in the issue and added log snippet.

jen: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-node-sdk/pull/234 (WIP). Notes: avoid JSON.stringify in retry-queue, parse on rehydrate fallback, add tests. Leaving TODO for careful audit of other middleware that serializes for telemetry.

maya: moving sampleapp to include the workaround for now, but removing before release once PR lands. Thanks! :thumbsup:

ryan: awesome. postmortem/notes: this is an onboarding friction story — newcomers copy sampleapp and hit schema validation errors with JSON mode, blame schema or model. let's add a short note in the JSON-mode guide about auth-retry parity and temporary workaround.

jen: agreed. I'll add a short blurb in docs and reference issue 1289.

maya: closing thread here; issue and PR linked. will follow up when PR merges.
